body:
### The problem

The common tokenizer continues a `//` comment on the next line when the line
ends with a backslash, as C does. In JavaScript a line comment always ends at
its line:

```js
function b(code) {
  return (
    code === 47 || // /
    code === 92 || // \
    code === 45 || // -
    code === 32
  )
}
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       7      3     19      1       8 b@1-8@a.js
```

The line after `// \` is read as part of the comment, so its `||` is lost: the
cyclomatic complexity of `b` is 3 instead of 4, and its NLOC 7 instead of 8.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_templates.py`, `lizard_languages/tsx.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript.py`. The pattern that already ends a line comment
inside the interpolations of a template, at any JavaScript line terminator, is
now shared with the JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX and TSX tokenizers. With the
fix:

```
       8      4     23      1       8 b@1-8@a.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_JavaScript_line_comment_ending_with_a_backslash` in
`test/test_languages/testJavaScript.py`, with subtests for .js, .ts, .jsx and
.tsx, which fail on `master` without the change. The full suite passes on the
branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1666 passed, 7 skipped. pycodestyle
reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

Line comments in C and C++, which keep the continuation after a backslash, and
block comments.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
title: End a JavaScript line comment at its line, also after a backslash
